desk.headline: Revenue up 66% on the prior quarter to $228m, ahead of estimates, as AI Cloud sales nearly tripled; $4bn+ run-rate target pushed to January
results: Total revenue rose 66% from the June quarter to $228m; AI Cloud revenue climbed to $200m from $71m, while Bitcoin mining fell to $28m from $67m as mining machines made way for GPUs.
AI Cloud segment gross margin (before depreciation) held at 86%; adjusted EBITDA rose to $66m (29% margin) from $19m.
The net loss narrowed to $263m from $684m, which had included a $450m impairment; depreciation rose to $148m.
Revenue backlog grew 22% to $20.3bn, about two-thirds with investment-grade customers; Horizon 1 went into service for Microsoft.
Heavy build-out: $4.8bn spent on property and computer hardware in the quarter, net debt rose to $4.4bn from $216m, and cash including restricted cash ended at $5.8bn.

guidance.summary: No revenue or earnings range. The more than $4bn annual run-rate target, earlier set for end-2026, is now aimed at January 2027 and could slip to end-February after a customer-requested design change and supplier timing. On the call, management guided cash operating costs up about $50–60m in the December quarter.

points: The run-rate delay came from Microsoft asking for upgraded network infrastructure on 200MW of capacity; management called the extra cost immaterial.
Pricing is rising: a new five-year deal at about $22m per MW with 90% of GPU capex prepaid, a short-term deal above $40m per MW, and older H100 GPUs re-contracted at double the old price.
About a quarter of the $1bn operating run rate at end-September is expected to show up as revenue in the December quarter, with little from new Horizon and Mackenzie capacity yet.
Capex plans were trimmed with cost of capital in mind; co-CEO Daniel Roberts said the company will not grow "at all costs".
Bitcoin mining is being wound down, with the switch to GPUs meant to be largely done by end-December.
call.source: Call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 6 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether the $4bn+ run rate is reached in January or slips to February.
Closing the $6bn funding gap for planned FY27 capex, and the terms.
December-quarter revenue as Horizon capacity is commissioned and mining revenue fades.
